title: Code of Virginia, Title 60.2 (Unemployment Compensation), Chapter 8 - Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance Program
verified_how: fetched https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title60.2/chapter8/ (HTTP 200): heading 'Chapter 8. Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance Program', listing s 60.2-800 (Definitions), 60.2-801 (Paid family and medical leave insurance program), 60.2-802 (Eligibility for benefits; certification), 60.2-803 (Duration of benefits), 60.2-804 (Amount of benefits), 60.2-805 (Family and Medical Leave Insurance Trust Fund), 60.2-806 (Contributions), 60.2-807, 60.2-808 (Leave and employment protection; remedies), 60.2-809, 60.2-810 and 60.2-811 onward, with no section marked 'Repealed' or '(Effective ...)'. I also fetched the individual section page https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/60.2-801/ (HTTP 200): breadcrumb 'Table of Contents > Title 60.2. Unemployment Compensation > Chapter 8. Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance Program > s 60.2-801', history line '2026, cc. 981, 1093'. Currency: the register's own 2026 Updates page (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacodeupdates/) states 'this is a list of updated sections that took effect on July 1, 2026, unless otherwise noted', so the online Code reflects the 2026 session. The site marks future text as '(Effective <date>)' and dead text as 'Repealed', and the cited provisions carry neither marker. Note that article-level URLs such as /vacode/title40.1/chapter3/article2/ return HTTP 200 with an EMPTY content pane, so the citable register page for an article is its chapter page, which prints the article heading and its section list.
notes: A HUMAN SHOULD CHECK the phase-in. The chapter is newly enacted (2026, cc. 981, 1093) and the register shows it in force with no '(Effective ...)' qualifier on any section, but contribution and benefit start dates for a new PFML programme are commonly fixed inside the section text or in an uncodified enactment clause that the codified page does not display. Virginia's other leave statutes, verified on https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title40.1/chapter3/, are Title 40.1 ch. 3 art. 2.1 (Paid Sick Leave, ss 40.1-33.3 to 40.1-33.6, in force since 2021 Sp. Sess. I, c. 449 but confined to home health workers - I fetched s 40.1-33.3 and its 'employee' definition is a home health worker averaging at least 20 hours a week or 90 hours a month), art. 2.1:1 (a broader Paid Sick Leave article, every section marked '(Effective July 1, 2027)') and art. 2.2 (Organ Donation Leave, ss 40.1-33.7 to 40.1-33.12). There is no Virginia statute requiring paid public holidays or paid vacation for private-sector employees.
